evidence: Hang Chieu Street, also known as Phố Hàng Chiếu, is a captivating thoroughfare nestled in the heart of the thirty-six streets and guilds area of the ancient Thăng Long imperial city. This historic street, originally situated next to the Eastern gateway of the imperial city, has been a bustling commercial hub for centuries.

The name Hang Chieu is derived from its former role as a stop for merchants carrying sedge mats from distant craft villages, who would make their way upstream on the Hồng Hà River to trade. As one walks down Hang Chieu Street, the faded yellow of the brick walls blending with the rustic color of the rolls of chiếu and tarpaulin mats stacked closely together immediately catches the eye.

This bustling scene is nestled amidst the hurried traffic, right next to the crowded sidewalk always packed with goods and a constant stream of people coming and going. Throughout its history, Hang Chieu Street has been a hub of commercial activity, with locals and travelers alike hurrying to and fro, eager to shop for rolls of packaging and closely packed blinds.
